author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
book_use: Chapter 18 — supports the distinction between fluent synthesis and trustworthy provenance; names confabulation and information-integrity risks while providing a bounded counterpoint rather than treating all AI retrieval as unreliable

title: ISO 668:2020 — Series 1 freight containers — Classification, dimensions and ratings
book_use: Chapter 9 — grounds the container example in a family of standardized dimensions and ratings rather than a single universal box; current edition is under review and has a 2022 amendment

title: ISO 1161 — Series 1 freight containers — Corner and intermediate fittings — Specifications
book_use: Chapter 9 — shows that intermodal compatibility depends on standardized connection points as well as outer dimensions; sixth edition is under publication as of September 2026

title: ISO 1496-1:2013 — Series 1 freight containers — Specification and testing — Part 1
book_use: Chapter 9 — adds the structural/testing layer required for international road-rail-sea interchange; current edition has a 2024 amendment

title: ISO 6346 — Freight containers — Coding, identification and marking
book_use: Chapter 9 — adds the information layer: consistent container identity, size/type coding, and markings; Edition 5 is under publication and will replace ISO 6346:2022

title: Patient handover from surgery to intensive care: using Formula 1 pit-stop and aviation models to improve safety and quality
book_use: Chapter 3 — grounds the edge-hunting argument in a documented cross-domain transfer at Great Ormond Street Hospital; the revised handover process was associated with fewer technical errors, fewer information omissions, and a modest reduction in handover time; supports analogy as a source of process questions, not proof that domains are interchangeable
